extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and practitioners interested in news credibility and media-rating services
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and scoring used by NewsGuard to evaluate the credibility and transparency of news and information websites, as summarized on the Wikipedia page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not repeatedly publish false or egregiously misleading content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does not repeatedly publish false or egregiously misleading content."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit criterion used by NewsGuard staff to flag sites that repeatedly publish false or egregiously misleading material. Appears as the first item in NewsGuard's list of rating criteria; failure on this point contributes to low overall score and a red icon. Examples in the article cite sites labeled unreliable (e.g., Breitbart, InfoWars) and note that NewsGuard issues corrections and can reverse ratings (e.g., MailOnline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathers and presents information responsibly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether a site follows responsible reporting practices in sourcing, attribution, verification, and context. This is a core editorial-quality criterion in NewsGuard's evaluation checklist used by its team of journalists and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has effective practices for correcting errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the site has mechanisms to acknowledge and correct mistakes (e.g., published corrections, transparent errata policies). This contributes to the site's trustworthiness in the Nutrition Label and can influence the overall score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: "Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether the site clearly distinguishes factual reporting from opinion or commentary. The article notes this standard was applied when NewsGuard downgraded The New York Times for not distinguishing sufficiently between opinion and fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids deceptive headlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates headline practices to ensure they are not misleading or clickbait that misrepresents article content. Violations can negatively affect the site's reliability/trustworthiness ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website discloses ownership and financing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses transparency about who owns and funds the site; disclosure (or lack thereof) informs judgments about potential biases and financial conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly labels advertising
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether paid content and advertisements are clearly identified so readers can distinguish editorial content from sponsored/promotional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals who's in charge, including possible conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reveals who's in charge, including possible conflicts of interest."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires disclosure of editorial leadership and potential conflicts of interest (e.g., owners, funders, editorial decision-makers). Transparency here affects perceived independence and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides names of content creators with contact or biographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: "The site provides the names of content creators, along with either contact or biographical information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether authorship is transparent (named writers) and whether the site supplies contact or biographical details for accountability and reader assessment of expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratings scale and band thresholds (0–100 and band meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard rates websites on a scale of 0 to 100. "A site rating above 75% indicates credibility, a site rating of 60-75% indicates 'credibility with exceptions', and a site rating below 60% indicates unreliability."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores are numeric (0–100) and translated into qualitative bands described on each site's 'Nutrition Label'. The page gives example scores (e.g., Fox News 69.5, Breitbart 49.5, The Washington Post 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratings broken down into reliability, trustworthiness, and financial conflict-of-interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratings are "broken down in terms of reliability, trustworthiness, and financial conflict of interest" and displayed in a site's 'Nutrition Label'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard's presentation includes component-level breakdowns (the Nutrition Label) and a color-coded icon (green for pass, red for low score). The label explains criteria in depth and is intended to show why a particular score was assigned. The founders cautioned the Nutrition Label should not be treated as an FDA-equivalent endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human expert review and advisory to sites
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard's team of journalists and editors rate websites and "attempts to advise sites that it labels as unreliable on how to come into compliance with its rating criteria."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural criterion: evaluations are performed by human experts (not solely automated), and NewsGuard may provide guidance to sites on corrective actions. The article notes this practice and gives the example of NewsGuard reversing a listing for MailOnline after discussions.
